detail: ^ConversionFailedError: Invalid image: the HEIF picture could not be decoded$
reason: CI runner only: its libheif 1.17 does not read the mif3 brand; libheif 1.23.6 in the worker image (Debian 13, measured) does, and the conversion there equals libheif's own decode to jpg, png and webp (tests/image-heif-decode.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: Invalid image: the HEIF picture could not be decoded$
reason: CI runner only: its libheif 1.17 does not read uncompressed images with row-aligned tiles; libheif 1.23.6 in the worker image (Debian 13, measured) does, and the conversion there equals libheif's own decode to jpg, png and webp (tests/image-heif-decode.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: Invalid image: the DDS picture could not be decoded$
reason: CI runner only: its ImageMagick 6 has no BC7 reader; ImageMagick 7.1 in the worker image decodes it to the pixels Pillow decodes (tests/image-dds-dx10.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: Invalid image: the PCX picture could not be decoded$
reason: The file is damaged by design (a buffer-overrun test file of Pillow's: its header gives 12 bytes per line for 88 eight-bit pixels); Pillow, ImageMagick 6 and ImageMagick 7 refuse it too.

detail: ^EmptyAudioInputError: The audio file holds no audio samples
reason: The file is a 44-byte WAV header whose data chunk holds no sample. For .aac (ADTS, a run of frames with no header) zero frames are zero bytes; for .m4a, .mp3, .opus and .ogg FFmpeg writes a few hundred bytes that ffprobe and ffmpeg cannot open. Only FLAC and WAV hold a stream of zero frames as a readable file.

detail: ^UnreadableArchiveError: Could not read the archive: it is the first part of a multi-volume set and the next volume, .+\.r00, is not part of the upload; upload all parts together as one archive\.$
reason: The file is the first volume of a RAR set (old numbering): the data of vols/bigfile.txt continues in rarfile-rar3-old.r00 and .r01, which the source project publishes as separate files that the corpus does not hold, so no reader can convert the one volume. The refusal names the missing volume (policy 56).

detail: ^DecompressionLimitError: PDF stream of object \d+ is a JBIG2 page of 100000 x 100000 pixels that decodes to 1250000000 bytes;
reason: The file is a decompression bomb by design (three JBIG2 content streams that each declare a 100,000 x 100,000 pixel page, 1.25 GB decoded); the native route refuses it from the page size in the first bytes of the stream, in milliseconds (policy 61).

detail: ^PayloadLimitError: The document prints \d+ pages; at most 500 are rendered to images in one request\.
reason: The report prints 4,181 to 4,874 pages (LibreOffice 24.2, by platform): drawing them as JPEG or PNG takes more than the job time limit on the shared runner and packs half a gigabyte, so the request is refused with the page count and the ways out (pages, or multiPageOutput first); every other target of the file converts (policy 44).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: Corrupt XLS: Workbook stream not found in CFBF container$
reason: The file went through a text-mode transfer (every LF byte has an inserted CR, 68,946 of them), which shifted the compound file's sector tables and directory, so it holds no readable stream; xlrd refuses it too and LibreOffice imports the bytes as text. With the inserted CRs taken out it is a BIFF8 workbook that converts to the cells xlrd reads (tests/xls-damaged-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: Corrupt XLS: Workbook stream not found in CFBF container$
reason: The file went through a text-mode transfer (every LF byte has an inserted CR, 1,803 of them), which shifted the compound file's sector tables and directory, so it holds no readable stream; xlrd refuses it too and LibreOffice imports the bytes as text. With the inserted CRs taken out it is a BIFF7 Book workbook that converts to the cells xlrd reads (tests/xls-damaged-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: Corrupt XLS: Workbook stream not found in CFBF container$
reason: The file is cut off at 1.5 MiB while its header places the first FAT sector at sector 7953 (63 FAT sectors are listed, none is in the file), so the compound file has no readable stream; xlrd refuses it too and LibreOffice imports the bytes as text (tests/xls-damaged-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: The PostScript interpreter rejected the \.ps file: Error: /invalidaccess in --put--
reason: The WordPerfect 6.1 font programs fill the Encoding array of a Type 3 font with integers (`0 1 255{Encoding exch 0 put}for`, where Widths was meant) and add glyphs after definefont. Ghostscript replaces such an Encoding with a rebuilt copy whose attributes are `r_type_attrs(pencoding) & a_readonly`, which has no write bit even when the original had one (zbfont.c, build_gs_font, with a_readonly defined in iref.h; unchanged from 10.02.1 to the development branch), so the next `Encoding 1 /1 put`, in the font that page 10 of 27 loads, stops with invalidaccess, with and without -dSAFER (the mechanism is read from that source; that the line is the cause is measured). With that one line filling Widths the file converts to its 27 pages (tests/postscript-real-file-refusals.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: The PostScript interpreter rejected the \.ps file: Error: /limitcheck in --setcolorspace--
reason: The QuickDraw GX driver declares CIE colour spaces with ranges of 0 to 65535 (`/RangeABC [0 65535 0 65535 0 65535]`, `/RangeLMN`). Ghostscript accepts a CIE parameter of at most 10000 (zcolor.c, MAX_CIE_RANGE and get_cie_param_array, unchanged from 10.02.1 to the development branch), so the first colour space of page 1 stops with limitcheck, with and without -dSAFER. With the two ranges set to 9999 the file converts to its 24 pages (tests/postscript-real-file-refusals.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: The page cannot be written as DXF: the PDF text layer has no text for most of its bitmap-font characters \(drawn as pictures\)\.$
reason: Every page but one is written, dashed and skewed strokes included (policy 79); page 28 draws 13 bitmap-font characters and the PDF text layer reads all 13 as spaces, so there is no text to write for them (tests/postscript-real-file-refusals.test.ts).

detail: ^CadGeometryUnavailableError: SVG input exceeds the 5242880-character limit\.$
reason: The geometry of the other 18 pages is read, dashed lines included (policy 79); the SVG Poppler draws for pages 17 and 18 is 8.1 and 7.1 MB, larger than the 5 MiB the geometry reader reads, which stays (tests/postscript-real-file-refusals.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: LibreOffice could not read the \.ppt file: it is damaged(, encrypted)? or not a valid PPT document\.$
reason: Damaged: its SlidePersistAtom refers to the persist id 131072 instead of 2 (two bytes swapped against the 9,728-byte `office-slideshow-single_coloured_page.ppt`, which converts), and no persist entry has that id. LibreOffice 24.2 and 26.8 refuse it and Apache POI HSLF 5.4.0 logs "no core ID for reference ID 131072" and skips the slide. The text is still read by the in-process reader (tests/ppt-persist-id-seed.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: LibreOffice could not read the \.ppt file: it is damaged(, encrypted)? or not a valid PPT document\.$
reason: Damaged: the master slide's drawing is overwritten from byte 14,263 with a record whose type is 0xFFFF and whose length is 0xFFFFFFFF, which runs past its container (9,230 bytes differ from `office-slideshow-text-margins.ppt`, which converts). LibreOffice 24.2 and 26.8 refuse it; Apache POI HSLF 5.4.0 reads its one slide and the text TEST1 to TEST4. The text is still read by the in-process reader (tests/ppt-persist-id-seed.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: LibreOffice could not read the \.ppt file: it is damaged(, encrypted)? or not a valid PPT document\.$
reason: Damaged: the header and first bytes of a SlidePersistAtom are overwritten with the characters `\E]\E]]]]]]` (11 bytes differ from `office-slideshow-49648.ppt`, which converts), so the slide list no longer parses. LibreOffice 24.2 and 26.8 refuse it; Apache POI HSLF 5.4.0 reads its one slide and the two lines of text. The text is still read by the in-process reader (tests/ppt-persist-id-seed.test.ts).

detail: ^LegacyOfficeFormatError: PowerPoint presentation: the compound file is malformed \(Corrupt CFBF container: the sector chain starting at sector 213 returns to sector 0\.\)\.$
reason: Damaged: the FAT chain of a stream returns to sector 0 (the chain from sector 213 reaches sector 0 again), so the compound file has no readable stream. Apache POI 5.4.0 refuses to open it (POIFSFileSystem: "Potential loop detected - Block 0 was already claimed but was just requested again"), LibreOffice 24.2.7 does not load it ("source file could not be loaded") and LibreOffice 26.8 opens the bytes as a text document, so no reader reads it as a presentation. The refusal names the loop (tests/ppt-cfb-sector-loop.test.ts).

detail: ^CorruptStreamError: Invalid PDF document: missing %PDF- header$
reason: Damaged beyond repair: a 277-byte fuzzer file whose header is `%PDFn` and whose trailer and cross-reference stream are cut into fragments. `qpdf --check` and a plain rewrite stop with "unable to find trailer dictionary while recovering damaged file", Poppler's pdfinfo exits 1, pdfium answers "Data format error", MuPDF cannot open it and PDF.js stops on an illegal character (tests/pdf-unrecoverable-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^(PdfTextGeometryError: PDF text geometry could not be read: Invalid PDF structure\.|PdfStructureError: Unable to determine PDF page count: invalid or corrupted PDF structure\.)$
reason: Damaged beyond repair: the trailer is gone and the objects hold braces and stray tokens where dictionaries should be. `qpdf --check` stops with "unable to find trailer dictionary while recovering damaged file", Poppler's pdfinfo exits 99, pdfium answers "Data format error", MuPDF repairs the file to zero pages and PDF.js throws InvalidPDFException (tests/pdf-unrecoverable-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^PdfTextGeometryError: PDF text geometry could not be read: Invalid PDF structure\.$
reason: Damaged beyond repair: 184 bytes: a catalog dictionary that is never closed and a content stream that declares 17,863 bytes and stops inside the dictionary of an inline image. `qpdf --check` stops with "unable to find trailer dictionary while recovering damaged file", Poppler's pdfinfo exits 1, pdfium answers "Data format error", MuPDF repairs it to zero pages and PDF.js throws InvalidPDFException (tests/pdf-unrecoverable-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^(PdfTextGeometryError: PDF text geometry could not be read: Invalid PDF structure\.|PdfStructureError: Unable to determine PDF page count: invalid or corrupted PDF structure\.)$
reason: Damaged beyond repair: qpdf recovers a trailer with no /Root ("unable to find any pages while recovering damaged file"), Poppler's pdfinfo cannot find a trailer dictionary, pdfium answers "Data format error", MuPDF repairs it to one page with no text and PDF.js throws InvalidPDFException (tests/pdf-unrecoverable-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^PdfTextGeometryError: PDF text geometry could not be read: Invalid Root reference\.$
reason: Damaged beyond repair: the only object stream lists itself ("self-referential object stream 3") and its dictionaries have lost their key names. `qpdf --check` stops with "unable to find page tree", Poppler's pdfinfo finds no catalog, pdfium answers "Data format error", MuPDF repairs it to zero pages and PDF.js throws InvalidPDFException (tests/pdf-unrecoverable-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^(PdfTextGeometryError: PDF text geometry could not be read: Invalid Root reference\.|PdfStructureError: Unable to determine PDF page count: invalid or corrupted PDF structure\.)$
reason: Damaged beyond repair: 92 bytes, a cross-reference stream of size 0 with no trailer keys. `qpdf --check` stops with "unable to find trailer dictionary while recovering damaged file", Poppler's pdfinfo finds no trailer, pdfium answers "Data format error", MuPDF cannot open it and PDF.js throws InvalidPDFException (tests/pdf-unrecoverable-real-files.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: There is no text to put on slides\.$
reason: The file holds no text: the body is six empty paragraphs and the three headers, three footers, footnotes and endnotes it carries are empty, so LibreOffice's plain-text export is white space only (tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: There is no text to put on slides\.$
reason: The file holds no text: the body is a content control with no content (its placeholder text lives in the glossary part, which no export prints) and an empty paragraph, so LibreOffice's plain-text export is white space only (tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: There is no text to put on slides\.$
reason: The file holds no text: its one header holds a picture and the body is empty, and LibreOffice's plain-text export writes nothing for a header or a picture (tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: There is no text to put on slides\.$
reason: The file holds no text: the body draws four pictures and the two headers hold no text, and LibreOffice's plain-text export writes nothing for a picture (tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts).

detail: ^ConversionFailedError: There is no text to put on slides\.$
reason: The body is empty; the only words are the header line "blabal" and the footer line "blabla", which LibreOffice's plain-text export does not write, and slides hold the text of the body (tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts).
